WHICH IS NOT A RUNNABLE PROGRAM. THAT IS DELIBERATE — SUBSTITUTE IT.

Two independently-managed installs, resolved by PATH order, and the second
arrives via a WindowsApps shim. AUTHORITATIVE FOR THIS CHECKOUT: `python`,
i.e. C:\Python314\python.exe — a direct install rather than a Store
redirector, and the interpreter every cost figure in README.md was measured
with. They are interchangeable TODAY (same pytest 9.0.3, both numpy-absent,
both resolving srmech from the worktree) and nothing keeps them that way.
These commands said `python3` from rc452 with only a prose note asking you to
substitute it. That is the shape this whole directory argues against: merged
unedited, it RUNS, under the interpreter the hooks were not tested with, and
says nothing. An unrunnable placeholder fails visibly instead — the harness
warns per invocation and continues. Same trade as the no-git-hook note below.
Print yours with
python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
Why it is load-bearing: `jpl_audit_gate` imports `tests/test_jpl_audit.py`,
which imports pytest, and `prose_currency_gate` re-enters pytest. Under an
interpreter without pytest the JPL hook FAILS OPEN with a loud note — correct
behaviour, and silent enough that you would keep believing you had a gate. The
check that catches it is
<your-python> tools/hooks/jpl_audit_gate.py --selftest      # exit 1 if it
# cannot load
Everything a hook re-enters (pytest, the ratchet) uses `sys.executable`, so
pinning the launcher pins the whole chain.
PATHS: $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is expanded by Claude Code before the command runs.
_git_pin: ⚠️ PIN THE GIT — OR ASK A QUESTION THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT. Measured at
rc454 on ONE clean tree at ONE commit:
git status --porcelain -- python/README.md CHANGELOG.md
Windows git 2.53.0  ->  0 modified
WSL2 git    2.34.1  ->  2 modified
git status --porcelain -- docs/srmech/python/srmech
Windows -> 0        WSL2 -> 324
derived_ledger_freshness.py
Windows -> exit 0   WSL2 -> exit 2, blocking all 581 ledger rows
The checkout has core.autocrlf=true in the WINDOWS user's global config: index
blobs are LF, working files CRLF, and WSL git does not read that config (a
different HOME), so it honestly reports every text file modified. Windows git
is the authority here — the worktree's own .git file holds a `D:/...` gitdir
that WSL git cannot open at all without GIT_DIR overrides.
Rather than pin a binary and break under a WSL agent, the hooks ask git for a
CONTENT difference (`diff HEAD --numstat --ignore-cr-at-eol`, dropping 0/0
rows) via _hooklib.dirty_paths. Measured identical under both gits — 0/0/0 for
the three queries above, and BOTH report `2  0  tools/hooks/README.md` for one
real planted two-line edit, so the instrument can still return otherwise.
SRMECH_HOOK_GIT=<path> forces a specific binary if you ever need it. Each
hook's --selftest prints which git and which interpreter answered.

hooks._why: Fires on any segment that INVOKES `git commit`, INCLUDING the option-carrying forms `git -C <dir> commit`, `git --no-pager commit` and `git -c k=v commit` — the first cut required the subcommand to be args[0] and all three escaped it silently. Every other Bash command exits at the ~0.15 s _hooklib floor without importing the audit. On the commit path it costs 4.1-4.9 s Windows-native (median 4.3) and 4.5-9.5 s on the WSL2 9p mount (median 5.4); the cost is a property of the MOUNT and both figures are in README.md rather than one being rounded into the other.

PreToolUse._why: MultiEdit added to the matcher at rc455 — sha256_routing_gate simulates a MultiEdit's whole edit list, and generated_file_edit_blocker reads `file_path`, which MultiEdit also carries.

Stop._order: Cheapest first, so a block on a fast predicate is reported before a slow one is paid: ssot 0.5 s, stale-native 0.8 s, jpl-audit 4.1-4.9 s Windows-native / 4.5-9.5 s WSL2-9p, derived-ledger 4.5-5.7 s, prose-currency ~0.46 s when no prose surface moved and ~14 s with all four armed, ratchet-recount 18-20 s. Every figure is mount-dependent; see the two-environment tables in README.md.

_no_git_pre_commit_hook: There is deliberately NO .git/hooks/pre-commit peer for jpl_audit_gate, and
that is a measurement rather than a preference. `core.hooksPath` on this
machine is `D:\GitHub\mlehaptics\.git\hooks` — a Windows path. WSL2 is the
standing build-subagent environment and cannot resolve it, so a git hook
installed there is a SILENT NO-OP from WSL: it does not run, it does not
warn, and the commit succeeds. A gate that silently does nothing is worse
than no gate, because it is believed. The PreToolUse(Bash) arm above covers
the same moment and reports through the same channel as every other hook.

_why: ripple-stamp-before-push blocks `git push` on an op-touching branch unless
tools/hooks/ripple_stamp.py recorded a green ~27-minute sweep at the current
HEAD. It collides with the standing quota discipline ('commit and push
incrementally'), which is why the [ripple-pending] escape token exists.
To enable: move this entry into hooks.PreToolUse under the Bash matcher.
